sleeve-gastrico-turquia.title: Gastric sleeve in Turkey: what to expect before, during and after
sleeve-gastrico-turquia.excerpt: An honest guide to eligibility criteria, length of hospital stay, eating in the first weeks and remote follow-up.
sleeve-gastrico-turquia.body:
Sleeve gastrectomy, known as the gastric sleeve, is one of the procedures that bring the most international patients to Istanbul. Before thinking about dates and flights, though, it's worth understanding how the decision is made and what happens at each stage of the journey.

Before the trip: eligibility comes from the assessment

No package replaces a medical assessment. The first step is to send your medical history, recent test results and information about previous treatments. The partner medical team reviews your case and tells you whether surgery is indicated — and if it isn't, that is an honest answer too.

Criteria such as body mass index, related conditions and previous treatment attempts are assessed individually. Be wary of anyone who promises approval before seeing your test results.

  • Medical history and current medications
  • Recent test results, if available
  • Previous surgeries, especially abdominal ones
  • Expectations and possible travel dates

During your stay in Istanbul

For bariatric surgery, the stay is usually between 7 and 12 days, but the exact itinerary is set by the medical team and sent to you in writing before you fly. It includes pre-operative tests, the hospital stay, check-up appointments and the discharge consultation.

Throughout your stay you have transfers between airport, hotel and hospital, an interpreter at consultations and a coordinator available in your language — including for anyone traveling with you.

Afterwards: eating and remote follow-up

The first weeks call for a careful, gradual return to food. You go home with written instructions from the responsible team, and follow-up continues remotely: the line to your coordinator and, when needed, to the medical team stays open.

Bariatric surgery is the start of a change in routine, not the end of treatment.

It's also a good idea to arrange local follow-up in your country, with a doctor and a nutritionist, for long-term check-ups.

Questions to ask before you decide

  • Who is the surgeon, and how much experience do they have with this procedure?
  • Which hospital will the surgery take place in, and what intensive care facilities does it have?
  • What is and isn't included in the quote?
  • How do you stay in touch with the medical team after you return home?

If you'd like to know whether you are a candidate, send us your information for a free initial assessment.

fue-ou-dhi.title: FUE or DHI: which hair transplant technique is right for you
fue-ou-dhi.excerpt: The real differences between the techniques, their effect on density, recovery time and how we assess the donor area before you travel.
fue-ou-dhi.body:
FUE and DHI are the two techniques mentioned most often when it comes to hair transplants in Turkey. Both use follicular units taken from the donor area — the main difference is how the hairs are implanted.

FUE: opening the channels and implanting

In FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction), follicular units are extracted one by one from the donor area. The surgeon then opens channels in the recipient area and implants the hairs. In the Sapphire FUE variant, the channels are opened with sapphire blades.

DHI: implanting with a pen

In DHI (Direct Hair Implantation), the hairs are implanted with a pen-shaped instrument that opens the channel and places the follicle in a single movement. The technique allows precise control over the angle and direction of each hair.

Which is better?

There is no single answer. The choice depends on factors assessed case by case:

  • Size of the area to be covered
  • Quality and capacity of the donor area
  • Hair characteristics (thickness, curl, color)
  • Hairline design and facial proportions

In some cases the team combines the techniques. What matters is that the recommendation comes after your photos have been reviewed, not from a price list.

How we assess the donor area before you travel

We ask for photos from specific angles — front, top, sides and back — and information about your history of hair loss and any treatments you have had. With this, the medical team estimates whether the donor area can support the expected result and recommends the technique.

A stay in Istanbul for a hair transplant is usually 3 to 4 days. The responsible team explains recovery, care in the first few days and how long it takes for the hair to grow, with written instructions.

Density promised before anyone has seen your donor area is a warning sign.

Would you like your case reviewed? Send us your photos — the initial assessment is free.

como-escolher-clinica-turquia.title: How to evaluate a clinic in Turkey without falling for exaggerated promises
como-escolher-clinica-turquia.excerpt: Accreditation, the doctor's registration number, a written contract and the warning signs every international patient should know.
como-escolher-clinica-turquia.body:
Turkey is home to leading hospitals and highly experienced professionals. It is also home to aggressive advertising, packages sold without an assessment and promises that are hard to keep. Learning to tell one from the other is the most important part of your research.

1. The institution's accreditation

Ask where the procedure will take place and whether the institution has international accreditation. Check that it has its own anesthesiology team and intensive care support when needed — information a serious partner provides without hesitation.

2. The doctor's name and registration

You have the right to know who will operate on you. Ask for the doctor's full name, specialty and professional registration number. Be wary when the answer is vague (“our team”) or when the professional only appears on the day of the procedure.

3. A written contract and quote

A reliable quote sets out what is included — procedure, hospital stay, accommodation, transfers, interpreting, follow-up appointments — and what isn't. Payment methods, deposit amounts and cancellation terms should also be in writing, with a receipt and a contract.

4. Assessment before price

Anyone offering a fixed package before seeing test results or photos is selling a product, not recommending a treatment. The medical assessment comes first; the quote follows from it.

Warning signs

  • Guaranteed results, or results compared with another patient's
  • Pressure to decide quickly (“today only”, “last spot”)
  • No explanation of risks and recovery
  • Difficulty finding out who the responsible doctor is
  • No follow-up plan after you return home
Any offer that sounds too good to be true deserves suspicion — including ours.

The role of a coordination company

Velurea does not perform procedures: we connect you with partner doctors and hospitals and take care of your entire journey. That's why we can — and should — share the recommended team's professional registration, credentials and track record before you make any decision. Meet our partner network.

roteiro-viagem-medica.title: A medical trip itinerary: 10 days in Istanbul, day by day
roteiro-viagem-medica.excerpt: From arrival at the airport to the discharge consultation — how we organize tests, surgery, rest and free time safely.
roteiro-viagem-medica.body:
A well-planned medical trip leaves little room for improvisation. Below is an example of how a stay of about ten days in Istanbul is organized — the actual length depends on the procedure and is set by the medical team.

Before you fly

Once the assessment is complete and the medical plan approved, we set the dates, book a hotel near the hospital and send you a written day-by-day itinerary. Citizens of Brazil, Portugal and most Latin American and European countries do not need a visa for short tourist stays, but we advise on the documents required for each country.

Day 1 — Arrival

Airport welcome and private transfer to the hotel. Your coordinator confirms the schedule for the coming days and is available for any questions — yours and those of anyone traveling with you.

Day 2 — Consultation and tests

An in-person consultation with the medical team and pre-operative tests, with an interpreter at your side. This is the time to ask everything about the procedure, risks and recovery.

Days 3 to 5 — Procedure and hospital stay

The procedure takes place at the partner hospital, followed by the hospital stay recommended by the team. Your coordinator supports your family and stays in constant contact.

Days 6 to 9 — Recovery

Back at the hotel, with check-up appointments according to the medical plan. This is time to rest: outings only with the team's approval and always following the instructions you've been given.

Day 10 — Discharge and return

Discharge consultation, written instructions and transfer to the airport. Follow-up continues remotely after you return home, with an open line to your coordinator and the responsible medical team.

What coordination always includes

  • Initial assessment and personalized guidance
  • Hotel booking near the hospital
  • VIP transfers between airport, hotel and hospital
  • Interpreting and in-person support
  • Post-operative support after you return home
